force_channel.advanced_reason: Can cancel a recording that is in progress.
force_channel.description: Tune a channel even if that means cancelling a recording in progress (FORCECH). Only differs from set_channel when every tuner is busy.

set_channel.description: Tune a channel (SETCH). The box must be on Live TV — send teleport_live_tv first and wait for LIVETV_READY. The reply is a CH_STATUS or CH_FAILED line.

set_channel_subchannel.description: Tune an over-the-air subchannel, e.g. 2.1 as SETCH 2 1.

teleport_live_tv.description: Jump straight to Live TV (TELEPORT LIVETV).

teleport_my_shows.description: Jump straight to My Shows (TELEPORT NOWPLAYING).

methods.notes: Advertised only while Network Remote Control is enabled, so finding it here also says the socket is open. `swversion` begins with the software version (for example 20.7.4 or 14.8); KEYBOARD needs 12.0 or later. Ignore instance names beginning "Proxy(" — those are relays re-advertising a real box. The same host usually also advertises `_tivo-device._tcp` (port 80), whose TXT carries the box's serial as TSN, plus `platform` and `platformname`; join on hostname to pick those up.

device.name: TiVo DVRs and Minis (Series 3 and later) — Network Remote
device.notes:
TiVo stopped selling DVR hardware on 1 October 2025 and now sells service only, leaving a large fleet of Series 3, Premiere, Roamio, Bolt and Edge DVRs and their Minis with no new hardware behind them. Each box carries a simple local remote-control socket that needs no account and no cloud: once the owner turns on Network Remote Control in the box's settings, it accepts plain ASCII commands on TCP 31339 that press remote buttons, type, jump to screens and tune channels, and it reports the current channel back as text.
The richer "Mind RPC" API (TLS on port 1413, `_tivo-mindrpc._tcp`) needs per-account credentials and is out of scope here; this spec is the remote-control socket only.
LINE PROTOCOL: every command is one line of ASCII ending in CR (0x0d). The box answers with lines of its own (see payload_formats). It sends a CH_STATUS line unprompted as soon as a client connects, whenever there is a current channel, and again on every channel change; a client can read the channel simply by connecting.

openness.notes: TiVo published the protocol for home-automation installers as a short PDF ("TiVo TCP Network Remote Control Protocol", v1.1). That PDF is no longer on tivo.com, so the facts here are transcribed from open-source clients built against it. The TiVoConnect discovery beacon is documented in TiVo's own 2003 specification.

credentials.notes: The socket has no authentication at all: anything on the LAN that can reach port 31339 can drive the box while the setting is on.

factory_reset.description: TiVo boxes offer "Restart or Reset" under Help in the on-screen menu, with several levels of reset. Nothing about the network remote needs a reset; it is recorded so a reader knows what a full reset costs.
factory_reset.effect: Clears the box's settings, and depending on the option chosen its recordings and guide data, and returns it to guided setup — which also turns Network Remote Control back off. Never needed for this protocol.

procedures.basis: TiVo Roamio Viewer's Manual (Help, Restart or Reset).
procedures.name: Restart or Reset menu

steps.action: From the TiVo menu choose Help, then Restart or Reset, then the reset level wanted.
steps.expect: The box reboots into guided setup.

methods.description: On a TiVo-branded box, open the TiVo menu, then Settings, then the remote / CableCARD / devices section, choose Network Remote Control and set it to enabled. Virgin Media boxes keep the same option under Help & Settings, then Settings, then Devices.
methods.name: Enable Network Remote Control

steps.action: On the box, go to Settings, then Remote, CableCARD & Devices, then Network Remote Control, and choose Enabled.
Browse mDNS for _tivo-remote._tcp, or connect to TCP 31339 on the box's address.
steps.expect: The connection opens; a CH_STATUS line arrives if the box is on Live TV.

setup.notes: The box itself is set up through its own on-screen guided setup; the one step this protocol needs is turning on Network Remote Control, which is off from the factory.

rejoin.notes: The box's own network settings change through its menus; the remote socket follows the box onto whatever network it joins.

testing.notes: Not driven against hardware by this project. The command set and replies are transcribed from two independent open-source clients (openHAB and McBrine's Network Remote) that agree on them.

entities.name: Channel
entities.notes: Sends SETCH. The current channel is read from the CH_STATUS line the box sends when a client connects (payload_formats.ChannelStatus); this transport has no request/response state read a consumer can bind.

entities.name: Standby
entities.notes: Toggles standby. From standby the box comes up in Live TV. No status line comes back.

evidence.documentation_review: openHAB's TiVo binding (README and the Java status provider and handler) and McBrine's Network Remote were read on 2026-10-11 and agree on the commands, the CR line ending, the single-client limit and the reply tokens. The discovery beacon facts are from TiVo's 2003 TiVoConnect specification, cross-checked against Wireshark's dissector and pyTivo. The mDNS TXT keys come from a 2011 Premiere sample and were not checked on newer boxes.
evidence.open_questions: The vendor PDF was not obtained. Whether a Mini, which has no tuner of its own, accepts SETCH; the CH_STATUS padding width per generation; and whether TELEPORT SEARCH and NETFLIX are official or later additions.

http_endpoints.description: Placeholder only, to satisfy the schema's access-surface rule. Control is ASCII lines over a raw TCP socket on port 31339 (see `commands` and protocol_details.tivo_network_remote), not HTTP.
http_endpoints.name: Local API Placeholder

ChannelFailed.description: CH_FAILED line, the answer to a SETCH/FORCECH (or a connect) that could not tune.
parse_rules: The token after CH_FAILED is the reason; look it up in values.

values.MALFORMED_CHANNEL: The channel argument did not parse.
values.MISSING_CHANNEL: Channel is not in the box's lineup.
values.NO_LIVE: Not on Live TV (or in standby); TELEPORT LIVETV first.
values.RECORDING: Every tuner is recording; SETCH refused (FORCECH would cancel one).

ChannelStatus.description: CH_STATUS line, sent on connect and on every channel change.

fields.description: Major channel number, zero-padded (four digits in openHAB's parser; an older Series 3 report shows three).
fields.name: channel

fields.description: Either the OTA subchannel (also zero-padded) or the reason token.
fields.name: subchannel_or_reason

fields.description: Last token: LOCAL (changed from the box itself), REMOTE (changed by an IR or IRCODE press) or RECORDING (the tuner is recording).
fields.name: reason

parse_rules: Split on spaces. Token 0 is CH_STATUS; token 1 is the channel with leading zeros; parse it as an integer rather than relying on its width.
If there are four tokens, token 2 is the subchannel and token 3 the reason; with three tokens, token 2 is the reason.

OtherReplies.description: The remaining lines a client sees.
parse_rules: Treat any other line as informational and keep reading.

values.COMMAND_TIMEOUT: Arrives unprompted a few seconds after a command; harmless, ignore it.
values.LIVETV_READY: Live TV is up, typically after TELEPORT LIVETV.

commands.FORCECH: FORCECH <channel> or FORCECH <major> <minor> — tune, cancelling a recording if every tuner is busy.
commands.IRCODE: IRCODE <key> — one remote button press; keys below.
commands.KEYBOARD: KEYBOARD <key> — one keyboard key; software 12.0 (Premiere) and later. Send LSHIFT first for the shifted character.
commands.SETCH: SETCH <channel> or SETCH <major> <minor> — tune; the box must be on Live TV, and it refuses if every tuner is recording.
commands.TELEPORT: TELEPORT <TIVO|LIVETV|GUIDE|NOWPLAYING> — jump to a screen. openHAB also sends SEARCH and NETFLIX, which are not in the original four.

tivo_network_remote.ircode_keys: UP DOWN LEFT RIGHT SELECT; TIVO LIVETV GUIDE INFO EXIT BACK; THUMBSUP THUMBSDOWN; CHANNELUP CHANNELDOWN; PLAY FORWARD REVERSE PAUSE SLOW REPLAY ADVANCE RECORD (STOP on DVD models); NUM0-NUM9 ENTER CLEAR; ACTION_A ACTION_B ACTION_C ACTION_D; CC_ON CC_OFF; WINDOW (the Zoom/Aspect/Window key across remote generations); ASPECT_CORRECTION_FULL ASPECT_CORRECTION_PANEL ASPECT_CORRECTION_ZOOM ASPECT_CORRECTION_WIDE_ZOOM; VIDEO_MODE_FIXED_480i VIDEO_MODE_FIXED_480p VIDEO_MODE_FIXED_720p VIDEO_MODE_FIXED_1080i VIDEO_MODE_HYBRID VIDEO_MODE_HYBRID_720p VIDEO_MODE_HYBRID_1080i VIDEO_MODE_NATIVE (these rewrite the video output setting); FIND_REMOTE; STANDBY; NETFLIX. Letters A-Z and MINUS EQUALS LBRACKET RBRACKET BACKSLASH SEMICOLON QUOTE COMMA PERIOD SLASH BACKQUOTE SPACE also work as IRCODE keys on current software, and are the KEYBOARD key set.
tivo_network_remote.liveness: An empty line (CR alone) draws INVALID_COMMAND and/or COMMAND_TIMEOUT, which proves the socket is alive.
tivo_network_remote.pacing: Clients pause 100-200 ms after each command (openHAB 200 ms, twice that after SETCH/FORCECH; McBrine 100 ms, plus 100 ms between KEYBOARD characters). No documented rate limit; bursts are where key presses get lost.
tivo_network_remote.single_client: One client at a time. While a connection is held open, phone apps and every other integration are locked out, so a client that only needs to send a command or read the channel should connect, act and disconnect. openHAB polls this way every 10 s by default.
tivo_network_remote.standby: In standby, TELEPORT does nothing useful; IRCODE TIVO (or IRCODE STANDBY, which toggles) wakes the box. CH_FAILED NO_LIVE is also what a box in standby answers to SETCH.
tivo_network_remote.transport: TCP 31339, ASCII lines. Send CR (0x0d) after each command; openHAB sends CR LF and works, McBrine sends CR alone.

tivoconnect_beacon.description: The older discovery path, documented by TiVo in 2003 and still sent by current boxes. A beacon is ASCII name=value lines separated by LF; the first line must be tivoconnect=1. Keys: method (broadcast or connected), platform (tcd/<series> for a DVR), machine (the box's name), identity (its TSN serial), services (comma-separated name[:port][/protocol]) and swversion. Unknown keys are ignored.
tivoconnect_beacon.example:
tivoconnect=1
method=broadcast
platform=tcd/Series4
machine=Living Room
identity=<tsn>
swversion=20.7.4
tivoconnect_beacon.tcp: Connect to TCP 2190, send one beacon, read one back. Working clients (pyTivo, McBrine) prefix each beacon with its length as a 4-byte big-endian integer, which the 2003 document does not mention.
tivoconnect_beacon.udp: Broadcast to UDP 2190: about every 5 s for 30 s after start-up or a change, then about once a minute. A client can simply listen.

remaining_unknowns: TiVo's own v1.1 protocol PDF could not be retrieved (vendor URL 404, no archive snapshot found on 2026-10-11); its Appendix A KEYBOARD table is therefore reconstructed from McBrine's client.
TiVo Mini behaviour: whether SETCH/FORCECH work (the Mini borrows a host DVR's tuner) or always answer CH_FAILED. No source covers it.
CH_STATUS channel padding: four digits in openHAB, three in an older Series 3 report.
Line-oriented TCP has no `commands.transport` value in the schema; these commands rely on `device.transport: tcp` and carry their CR terminator in `body`.
